title: Terraform Variables, Outputs, and Locals
subtitle: Inputs, internal values, and outputs for reusable Terraform patterns

nodes.label: Variables
nodes.definition: Variables are input values passed into Terraform configuration.
nodes.whyItMatters: Variables make Terraform reusable instead of hardcoding every value.
nodes.safeSentence: Variables let the same Terraform code work with different inputs.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not hardcode environment-specific values everywhere when variables would make the configuration cleaner.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Variables are Terraform inputs. They let teams reuse the same configuration with different values for environment, size, region, names, or settings.

note.summary:
Variables are how Terraform accepts input.

Instead of hardcoding bucket names, pass values for dev/test/prod.

Tiny example:
variable "bucket_name" {
  type = string
}

Use in resource: bucket = var.bucket_name

image.caption: Variables/tfvars flow into config, locals, resources, and outputs across environments.

nodes.label: Variable Types
nodes.definition: Variable types define what kind of value a variable accepts.
nodes.whyItMatters: Types help catch mistakes and document what values are expected.
nodes.safeSentence: Variable types make Terraform inputs clearer and safer.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not leave every input untyped in serious team configurations.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Variable types help Terraform validate inputs such as string, number, bool, list, map, or object.

nodes.label: Defaults
nodes.definition: A default is the fallback value Terraform uses when no value is supplied.
nodes.whyItMatters: Defaults make simple use cases easier, but important settings still need review.
nodes.safeSentence: Defaults are useful, but environment-specific values should be chosen carefully.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not hide important production choices behind casual defaults.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Defaults make variables optional, but teams should be careful when defaults affect important infrastructure behavior.

nodes.label: tfvars
nodes.definition: tfvars files provide values for Terraform variables.
nodes.whyItMatters: They separate reusable Terraform logic from environment-specific inputs.
nodes.safeSentence: tfvars files let teams keep variable values separate from reusable configuration.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not commit secret values in tfvars files.
nodes.interviewAnswer: tfvars files are commonly used to provide environment-specific variable values without changing the main Terraform code.

note.summary:
Example dev.tfvars:
environment = "dev"
bucket_name = "dev-learning-logs"

Conceptual usage: terraform plan -var-file="dev.tfvars"

nodes.label: Sensitive Values
nodes.definition: Sensitive values are inputs or outputs that should be hidden from casual display.
nodes.whyItMatters: Terraform configurations may handle secrets, tokens, passwords, or IDs that need protection.
nodes.safeSentence: Sensitive values need careful handling and should not be casually committed or exposed.
nodes.commonTrap: Marking a variable sensitive does not mean all risk disappears; state may still contain sensitive data.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Sensitive variables help reduce accidental exposure, but Terraform state and outputs still need access control.

nodes.label: Locals
nodes.definition: Locals are internal named expressions used inside Terraform configuration.
nodes.whyItMatters: Locals reduce repetition and make calculated values easier to read.
nodes.safeSentence: Locals help avoid repeating the same expression across Terraform files.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not overuse locals until the configuration becomes hard to follow.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Locals are reusable internal values. They are not inputs from outside; they are computed inside the Terraform configuration.

nodes.label: Outputs
nodes.definition: Outputs expose useful values after Terraform evaluates or creates resources.
nodes.whyItMatters: Outputs help people and downstream automation see important resulting values.
nodes.safeSentence: Outputs make important Terraform results visible.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not expose secrets or sensitive values casually through outputs.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Outputs can expose values like names, IDs, URLs, endpoints, or generated resource attributes.

nodes.label: Naming Patterns
nodes.definition: Naming patterns keep Terraform inputs and outputs consistent and readable.
nodes.whyItMatters: Consistent names make Terraform easier to review and maintain.
nodes.safeSentence: Good naming patterns make Terraform code easier for teams to understand.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not create clever names that hide what the variable or output really means.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Naming patterns matter because Terraform is reviewed as code, and clear names reduce confusion.

note.summary:
Good examples: environment, region, bucket_name, owner_tag, common_tags.
Avoid: x, data1, temp_value.

nodes.label: Environment Inputs
nodes.definition: Environment inputs are different variable values for dev, test, stage, or prod.
nodes.whyItMatters: They let the same Terraform pattern behave differently across environments.
nodes.safeSentence: Variables help the same Terraform code support different environments safely.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not mix production and development values accidentally.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Environment inputs help teams reuse Terraform patterns while keeping dev, test, and production settings separate.

note.summary: dev.tfvars vs prod.tfvars can vary size/tags/names while code stays the same.

nodes.label: Reuse Pattern
nodes.definition: The reuse pattern combines variables, locals, and outputs to make Terraform configuration flexible and understandable.
nodes.whyItMatters: This is how Terraform grows from one-off examples into reusable infrastructure patterns.
nodes.safeSentence: Variables, locals, and outputs are the basic ingredients of reusable Terraform.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not jump to modules before understanding inputs, internal values, and outputs.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Variables provide inputs, locals organize internal expressions, and outputs expose useful results. Together they make Terraform code reusable.

note.summary: Flow: variables in -> locals standardize -> resources manage -> outputs expose. This bridges naturally to modules.

nodes.label: Terraform Core Workflow
nodes.definition: Open the previous map that explains the practical Terraform workflow.
nodes.whyItMatters: Variables, locals, and outputs make more sense when connected to init, validate, plan, and apply.
nodes.safeSentence: Inputs and outputs are part of the Terraform workflow because they affect what plan and apply will do.
nodes.commonTrap: Do not treat this as a variable concept. It is a map doorway.
nodes.interviewAnswer: Variables and outputs fit into the workflow because they influence the plan and make resulting infrastructure values visible.
